actions.action: In Coordination research / First conversation, use @ to read the saved File-check reminder replication draft v2. Ask for a Markdown summary without changing or running anything.
Ask the guide to create a new experiment plan from the editable copy: two teams per condition, six rounds, valid probability 0.35, assignment seed 61006. Do not build or run yet.
Ask the guide to build and review a real shared-file simulator from the new exact plan, without running subjects.
Ask the guide to run the new experiment with real LLM subjects. Switch to another chat while it works, and keep a separate unsent question there.
Return to First conversation. Ask for the new result in simple Markdown with charts. Check stored effects and uncertainty; do not assume the reminder helped.
Ask to replay the earlier experiment-b62705a33765 v1 from another project using @. Scrub backwards and forwards and return. The new plan and old immutable outcome should remain available.
Ask to reuse an exact older plan, then fork this chat to explore another idea. Keep original objects unchanged; branch history and future state must be independent.
Reload the branch, switch back to First conversation and inspect its own saved state. Exact citations, the new experiment, original draft and guide operation receipts should remain accessible.

predictions.goal: Test persistent project/chat behavior, guide operation workflow, shared-file simulator creation, running experiments with LLM subjects, cross-chat switching, Markdown rendering, replay/reuse/branch behavior, and reload/resume state integrity in a local Society Lab.
limitations: This is UI/functional testing only, not validation of any scientific theory or treatment effect.
Do not assume the reminder or draft changes experimental outcomes.
Predictions are about observable app behavior, not hidden implementation details.
Keep exact step order and IDs.
Separate original, branched, reused, and replayed objects conceptually; expect them to remain independently accessible if the product supports it.

steps.belief: The app will likely allow reading the saved replication draft via @ in the First conversation and return a Markdown-formatted summary without modifying state or starting execution.
checks: The draft v2 content is rendered or summarized in Markdown.
No new run/build status appears.
No changes are made to the draft contents or timestamps beyond read access, if tracked.
The conversation remains the same thread/project.
failure_signals: @ mention fails to resolve the saved draft.
The UI edits or starts running the draft unexpectedly.
Markdown is not rendered or summary is plain/unformatted when Markdown is requested.
The saved draft becomes inaccessible after read.

steps.belief: The guide will create a new experiment plan from the editable copy, likely preserving the requested parameters: two teams per condition, six rounds, valid probability 0.35, assignment seed 61006, without building or running yet.
checks: A new plan object appears in saved state.
The plan reflects two teams per condition, six rounds, probability 0.35, and seed 61006.
No simulator/build artifacts are created yet.
The editable copy remains intact as a separate object.
failure_signals: Plan parameters are changed or partially ignored.
The system immediately builds or runs instead of only saving the plan.
The original editable copy is overwritten.
The plan cannot be created from the editable copy.

steps.belief: The guide will build a real shared-file simulator from the new exact plan and provide a review/confirmation, while the subjects are not run yet.
checks: A simulator/world artifact is created from the saved plan.
Review details are shown for the simulator configuration.
No subject run results are present yet.
The simulator corresponds to the exact plan parameters.
failure_signals: Build triggers an experiment run prematurely.
The created simulator diverges from the requested plan.
Review output is missing or the build fails.
The saved plan is modified instead of used as input.

steps.belief: The app will start running the experiment with real LLM subjects, and switching to another chat should preserve a separate unsent question there while the run continues in the background or queued state.
checks: Run status/progress is visible for the new experiment.
The user can navigate to another chat without losing the run.
An unsent draft/question remains in the other chat.
Returning later should still show the run or its completion state.
failure_signals: Run cannot start or blocks chat switching.
Switching chats discards the unsent question.
The run is canceled or detached when changing conversations.
Background progress is not preserved.

steps.belief: Returning to First conversation should expose the new result in simple Markdown with charts, plus stored effects and uncertainty, without implying the reminder caused the outcome.
checks: Result is shown in the First conversation.
Output is in simple Markdown and includes charts/visual summaries if supported.
Stored effects and uncertainty are explicitly displayed or accessible.
Language does not attribute causal influence to the reminder.
failure_signals: Results are missing or not linked to the run.
Markdown/charts are not rendered as requested.
Uncertainty/effect storage cannot be inspected.
The UI or text incorrectly claims the reminder caused the result.

steps.belief: The system will be able to replay the earlier experiment-b62705a33765 v1 from another project using @, and after scrub backward/forward plus return, the old immutable outcome and the new plan should both remain available.
checks: The old experiment is accessible via @ from another project.
Replay controls allow scrubbing backward and forward.
Returning restores the current context.
Both old immutable outcome and new plan remain accessible afterward.
failure_signals: The old experiment cannot be found or replayed.
Scrubbing changes the underlying immutable result.
Returning loses the new plan or current context.
Cross-project access via @ fails.

steps.belief: The app will support reusing an exact older plan and forking the chat into a separate branch so original objects remain unchanged and histories/future state diverge independently.
checks: An exact older plan can be reused without mutation.
A branch/fork of the chat is created.
Original objects remain unchanged after branching.
Branch history and future state differ independently from the source.
failure_signals: Reuse mutates the source plan.
Forking is unavailable or collapses into the same history.
Branch and source share the same future state unexpectedly.
Older plan contents change after reuse.

steps.belief: Reloading the branch and switching back to First conversation should preserve access to saved state, exact citations, the new experiment, the original draft, and guide operation receipts.
checks: Reload returns to the branched conversation state.
Switching back to First conversation works after reload.
Exact citations are still available.
The new experiment, original draft, and guide operation receipts remain accessible.
failure_signals: Reload loses branch state or citations.
Switching back to First conversation fails.
Saved artifacts disappear after reload.
Guide operation receipts are missing or corrupted.

scope: Functional product behavior; subjective agent predictions are not observed results.
